chapters.name: THE SHOT
chapters.title: A world in motion.
chapters.subtitle: Ten seconds. One continuous camera move.
chapters.detail: Original procedural scene · Blender Cycles · 240 individually rendered frames

chapters.name: 01 / MOVING WATER
chapters.title: Give the waves a clock.
chapters.subtitle: Four traveling waves move the actual surface mesh.
chapters.detail: Dispersion-inspired waves with an artistic time scale; fine shader normals drift separately.

chapters.name: 02 / DRIFTING MIST
chapters.title: Move a field through the light.
chapters.subtitle: The density changes in space and drifts over time.
chapters.detail: g is Generated space; N is 3D noise (detail 4, roughness 0.66). R(n) = 0.18 + 1.10 clip((n−0.18)/0.60, 0, 1). Procedural advection; no fluid simulation.

chapters.name: 03 / WET STONE
chapters.title: Let the waterline shape the surface.
chapters.subtitle: Lower stone is smoother and more strongly coated.
chapters.detail: z is world-space height. This authored wetness gradient is applied to the two added foreground stones.

chapters.name: 04 / THE CAMERA
chapters.title: A smooth path through the inlet.
chapters.subtitle: Foreground stone passes faster than the distant stacks.
chapters.detail: 32.5 mm lens · f/7.1. A moving look-at target keeps the inlet composed. Lengths are scene units.

disclosure: Same ten-second 3D-rendered shot replayed for four mathematical explanations. No optical-flow interpolation or image warping.
